text: In the memory-capacity lab, how does the per-delay profile MC_k change as rho goes from 0.5 to 0.99?
choices: At rho = 0.5 MC_k decays rapidly (memory at short delays); at rho = 0.99 it decays slowly, spreading memory over many delays
At rho = 0.5 MC_k is flat, while at rho = 0.99 it is a single sharp spike
MC_k is identical for both, because total MC is bounded by N
At rho = 0.5 MC_k decays slowly, while at rho = 0.99 it decays rapidly
explanation: Since MC_k ~ rho^(2k), a small rho (0.5) makes memory decay quickly and stay concentrated at short delays with total MC well below N, whereas rho = 0.99 decays slowly, spreading appreciable memory across many delays so total MC approaches N. Option D reverses this direction; the bound MC <= N does not make the profiles equal.
